chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Marwan, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to fast until it was said he does not break his fast. Then he would fast for a day and break his fast on another day. Then he would fast on Monday and Thursday. Then it settled into fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he used to say, 'That is the fasting of the year (perpetual fasting).'
And my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'No one is more detestable to me than a man who is told that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to do so-and-so, and he says,

key_terms.الْإِثْنَیْنِ وَ الْخَمِیسَ: Monday and Thursday (common days for voluntary fasting)
key_terms.صَوْمُ الدَّهْرِ: Perpetual fasting (fasting every day of the year)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended pattern of voluntary fasting in a month according to the Prophet (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) gradual transition from continuous fasting to the specific pattern of fasting the first Thursday, middle Wednesday, and last Thursday of the month, which he designated as 'Sawm al-Dahr' (fasting of the year). This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the virtue of these specific days and serves as a critique against those who selectively follow the Prophet’s practices, arguing that his voluntary acts were not due to inability but rather to demonstrate the fullness of his spiritual excellence.
